_run_state_note: M8-056: a run only becomes UNKNOWN through a reported non-ok native end, and only a DOCUMENTED transient failure class (RUN_TIMEOUT, TRANSIENT_RUNTIME_FAILURE) may be reconciled, which stamps it FAILED. Every other failure class has no retry path and must be escalated. UNKNOWN -> FAILED is therefore the only edge out of UNKNOWN, and a superseded attempt (a higher attempt exists for the same node and brief revision) is terminal wherever it sits.
_correction_note: M12/T9 F-229: this projection was CORRECTED to match the reducer instead of being left to contradict it (which is what its own _note demands). Measured at HEAD against every `task.workflow_status = `, `task.brief_state = ` and `run.run_state = ` write in topology/lib/workflow.mjs, it was missing: ACTIVE -> REVISING (an approval that requests a revision), ACTIVE -> RESULT_PENDING_REVIEW (the root result), ACTIVE -> COMPLETE/PARTIAL/FAILED (the anchored pre-verdict root-result arm), RESULT_PENDING_REVIEW -> PARTIAL/FAILED (the post-ACCEPT status is DERIVED from the accepted outcome), REVISING -> REVISING (a revision requested while a revision is open), BLOCKED -> WAITING_FOR_USER/RESULT_PENDING_REVIEW/REVISING (a reconciled attempt restores the status it suspended) and SPAWN_UNKNOWN -> FAILED (an abandoned spawn is reconciled). The projection is still NOT enforced at the write seam: enforcing an INCOMPLETE projection would refuse a legitimate transition and make the live ledger unreadable, so the completeness proof is an owner decision (see the report). ONE divergence is left in place on purpose: the reducer's cancellation moves an UNKNOWN run to CANCELLED, while the tracked lane (tests/m7-lane-g-policy.test.mjs) pins this row to exactly [FAILED]. That pin is not this agent's to change, so the divergence is reported instead of being papered over.
